Amritesh Jatia Vs. Vidhi Jatia & Anr. Page No.1 of 16
 Judgment
1. Vide this order, I shall dispose of the appeal filed by the appellant / husband under provisions of Section 29 of The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (hereinafter referred as DV Act) assailing the impugned order dated 16.12.2023 passed by learned MM-02 (Mahila Court),
South District, Saket, New Delhi, in complaint case bearing CT Cases No.2345/2023 titled as Vidhi Jatia & Anr. Vs. Amritesh Jatia & Anr.. 
2. Vide impugned order dated 16.12.2023, learned MM while deciding the application under Section Amritesh Jatia vs Vidhi Jatia on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124618478/
1 23 DV Act filed by the complainant / wife (respondent no.1 herein) for grant of ex-parte relief,
restrained the appellant and his parents from forcibly dispossessing the complainant / applicant from the shared household i.e. 2nd Floor, B-50, Gulmohar Park, South Delhi. Learned MM further directed the appellant to remove his belongings from shared household and also restrained him from entering the second floor of the shared household till further orders. Appellant and his parents are also restrained from causing any domestic violence to the complainant and her children till further orders. 
3. Before adverting to the appeal, it is necessary to narrate the relevant facts which in nutshell are that the marriage between the parties was solemnized on 18.02.2010 in Phuket, Thailand as per Hindu rites and customs. Out of this wedlock, two children Amritesh Jatia Vs. Vidhi Jatia & Anr.
Page No.2 of 16 Aadidev (son) and Adira (daughter) were born on 23.01.2015 and 18.05.2019,
respectively, in London, UK and are British citizens. The marriage of the parties is replete with gross emotional verbal and economic abuse and neglect and when their relationship got strained,
respondent no.1 /complainant filed a petition under Section 12 of the DV Act before the learned trial court alleging therein various incidents of immense cruelty, emotional abuse, physical and mental abuse, economic abuse and psychological abuse inflicted upon her by the appellant. She has alleged that appellant has willfully neglected, abused and demeaned the respondents and son Aadidev and also refused to maintain and provide them adequately as per the lifestyle and status. She has further alleged various specific instances and incidents of domestic violence perpetrated by appellant on her and her children. Alongwith the complaint, an application under Section 23 (2) of DV Act was also filed by respondent no.1 / complainant seeking relief under Sections 18, 19, 20 and 22 of the DV Act. 
Upon receipt of the complaint, learned trial court called for Domestic Incident Report (DIR) and thereafter, after considering the submissions and material placed on record, granted ex-parte relief to respondent no.1 and restrained the appellant from forcibly dispossessing the complainant /
respondent no.1 from shared household and also summoned the appellant and his parents. 
Aggrieved by the order of learned MM granting ex-parte relief to Amritesh Jatia Vs. Vidhi Jatia &
Anr. Page No.3 of 16 respondent no.1, the appellant herein has preferred the present appeal. 
4. The appellant has assailed the impugned order on the grounds that :
a) learned MM without giving an opportunity to the opposite party to be heard erroneously passed the impugned order and respondent no.1 has maliciously concealed the facts to mislead the learned MM and fraudulently obtained ex-parte reliefs to harass the appellant ;
b) learned MM while granting ex-parte ad interim relief should have convinced herself that there is urgency in the matter which she has failed to do ;
c) learned MM has manifestly erred in relying on the order dated 04.11.2023 passed by Hon'ble High Court wherein it has been specifically mentioned that "the action of MCD will not prejudice any matrimonial proceeding between the parties" ;
Amritesh Jatia vs Vidhi Jatia on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124618478/
2 d) learned MM has failed to consider that respondent no.1 has not made a single averment in her complaint to show that there is an urgency for ex-parte relief ;
e) learned MM has failed to consider that respondent no.1 has failed to disclose that appellant and respondent no.1 were mediating for almost 2 years before Delhi High Court Mediation Centre and when appellant failed to fulfill the exorbitant monetary demands, respondent no.1 filed this DV complaint ;
Amritesh Jatia Vs. Vidhi Jatia & Anr. Page No.4 of 16 f) learned MM has failed to appreciate that respondent no.1 deliberately did not disclose the fact that the said property against which the respondent no.1 has asked for an ex-parte relief, is co- owned by Mrs. Archana Jatia and appellant is merely licensee in the property ;
g) learned MM erred in ignoring that respondent no.1 has purposely not filed the site plan of 2 nd floor as it would evidently shows that appellant also resides at the 2 nd floor and had his belongings therein ;
h) learned MM has also failed to consider that effect of ousting the appellant from his own floor of the said property would also effect his custody and access to the children ;
I) learned MM has failed to take into account that appellant has no other accommodation other than 2nd floor and he would be unable to shift his personal belonging to any other place ;
j) learned MM has erroneously passed the impugned order whereas, respondent no.1 has absolutely no prima facie case of domestic violence and all the allegations levied by her seems to be concocted ;
k) learned MM has failed to consider that the present proceedings are nothing but an abuse of process of law by respondent no.1 who has also dragged the minor children in this frivolous and falsified litigation without any rhyme or reason ;
l) learned MM has erred in ignoring that respondent no.1 has not Amritesh Jatia Vs. Vidhi Jatia &
Anr. Page No.5 of 16 filed the complaint under DV Act in terms of the provisions Order XXXII Rule 1 of CPC ;
m) learned MM has failed to appreciate that the sole aim of respondent no.1 is to mentally harass,
arm twist and coerce the appellant to concede to her exorbitant and malafide monetary demands ;
n) learned MM has failed to appreciate that the DV Act complaint is a clear afterthought and counterblast to the developments in the divorce proceedings pending adjudication between the parties and respondent no.1 intentionally concealed the same before the trial court ;
o) learned MM has also failed to consider that respondent no.1 has made serious and heinous allegations against the appellant and his parents without any timeline, date, place and specific Amritesh Jatia vs Vidhi Jatia on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124618478/
3 details to establish a prima facie case of domestic violence and further, the allegation of not giving food are not only noxious but also misconceived and strict action of perjury against respondent no.1.
5. Learned Senior counsel for the appellant has argued that the complaint filed by respondent no.1 before the trial court is ex-facie vague and bereft of any material particulars of any incident of alleged domestic violence. The order of learned MM for providing food has been passed without cause and is contrary to the record since there is no allegation in the complaint that the respondent at any time was deprived of food. Further, there is no averment Amritesh Jatia Vs. Vidhi Jatia &
Anr. Page No.6 of 16 stating any threat of dispossession made to the respondent no.1. Learned Senior counsel has also argued that learned MM has grossly erred in passing the impugned order by misplaced her reliance on order of Hon'ble High Court passed in W.P. (C) No.14454 of 2023 titled as Baby Adira Jatia & Ors. Vs. Municipal Corporation of Delhi & Ors. whereas, the appellant and his parents were equally aggrieved by the sealing action of MCD as MCD officials have also sealed other portions of the house and have denied access to their own property and belongings. It has further been argued that there is not even a single averment in the complaint that shows urgency for passing of such a drastic, peremptory and perfunctory order. Learned Senior counsel argued that the order passed by the trial court is fundamentally flawed as it fails to establish a prima facie case of domestic violence. Learned senior counsel stated that learned MM could have protected the rights of the respondent by directing provision of alternative accommodation instead of trampling over the rights of the appellant and his senior citizen parents and even the appellant is ready and willing to offer and provide alternate accommodation to the respondent commensurate to the lifestyle of the parties before separation. It has also been argued that respondent no.1 has intentionally concealed the fact of ongoing mediation efforts, which highlights that the parties were attempting to resolve their disputes amicably. This deliberate omission indicates bad faith and Amritesh Jatia Vs. Vidhi Jatia &
Anr. Page No.7 of 16 undermines the credibility of the respondent's claims. Learned counsel argued that the proceedings initiated by the respondent appear to be an abuse of process, aimed primarily at coercing the appellant into compliance with her financial demands. Furthermore, learned MM has granted ex-parte relief without adequately assessing the urgency of the situation. Respondent no.1 has failed to provide any compelling evidence indicating an immediate threat or harm that necessitated such urgent measures. The absence of urgency undermines the basis for ex-parte relief,
which should only be granted in genuine emergencies. It has been stated that by ousting the appellant from his residence, the court inadvertently affects his custody and access rights, which is contrary to the best interests of the children. This oversight further illustrates the lack of thorough evaluation in granting relief. Learned counsel emphasized that from the facts and circumstances, it is clear that the order issued by the trial court is completely arbitrary, illegal and contrary to the principles of law. Therefore, the same be set aside and appeal be allowed. In support of her submissions, learned senior counsel has placed reliance upon the following judgments :
a) Rajinder Singh Saluja Vs. Sarbjyot Kaur Saluja, FAO (OS) No.119/2008 dated 14.05.2009 ;
b) Eveneet Singh Vs. Prashant Chaudhary & Ors., CS (OS) No.1307/2010 dated 20.12.2010 ;
Amritesh Jatia vs Vidhi Jatia on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124618478/
4 Amritesh Jatia Vs. Vidhi Jatia & Anr. Page No.8 of 16 c) Shumita Didi Sandhu Vs. Sanjay Singh Sandhu & Ors. 2010 SCC OnLine Del. 3727 ; 
d) Vrinda Ahuja Vs. Raveen Ahuja, 2019 SCC OnLine Del.
11275 6. The respondent has duly contested the appeal. Rebutting the arguments addressed on behalf of the appellant, learned counsel for the respondent has argued that learned MM has passed a well- reasoned order and there is no reason to interfere in the same. It has been stated that the learned MM has rightly granted ad interim protection. On merits, it has been stated that the appeal deserves to be dismissed for want of non-joinder of necessary parties. It has been stated that appellant's parents are parties to DV proceedings and they have also been summoned by learned MM vide impugned order dated 16.12.2023 but they are neither parties to this appeal nor they have challenged the order of learned MM. Therefore, appellant's mother being owner of 2/3rd of the property has no objection to the protection order granted to the respondent no.1 and the children. 
Learned counsel also argued that the grounds sought to be espoused by appellant qua his parents is of no avail as they have not challenged the impugned order being parties in DV proceedings. 
Learned counsel further argued that the real intention of the appellant is to throw out the respondent no.1 and children from the shared household. Whereas, the respondent no.1 and children have a right to live with dignity in the shared household Amritesh Jatia Vs. Vidhi Jatia &
Anr. Page No.9 of 16 which includes a right to privacy and peace and a right to food. It has also been stated that the appellant has not come to the court with clean hands and has misrepresented to this court and the present appeal is nothing but an abuse of the process of law. The appellant has not been ousted from the shared household nor has he been rendered roofless. It has been stated that it is not the case of the appellant that when he filed the present appeal he was not staying in the shared household. The same is borne out from the affidavit filed by the appellant in support of the appeal wherein he has asserted that he is a resident of B-50, Gulmohar Park. The appellant has misrepresented that the 2 nd floor of the shared household is a separate unit however, there is a common kitchen and living room on the ground floor of property and some room bedrooms on the first floor, a puja room on the mezzanine floor and children' bedroom and respondent no.1's bedroom and maids rooms are on the other side of 2nd floor. Learned counsel stated that appellant himself has moved out of the bedroom on the 2 nd floor sometime in February 2023 and has been staying on the first floor of the shared household. Only the belongings and clothing of the appellant remained in his walk-in-closet on the 2nd floor and he has further affirmed that the entire house is one unit in his divorce petition. It has been argued that learned MM has recorded his findings as to the urgency in the matter and has rightly passed the impugned order granting ex-parte relief. With respect to sealing of Amritesh Jatia Vs. Vidhi Jatia & Anr. Page No.10 of 16 property by MCD, it has been stated that on 03.11.2023 MCD officials came to seal the basement and 2 nd floor and only on the filing of Writ Petition before Hon'ble High Court on an urgent basis the matter was specially listed on 04.11.2023 wherein the Hon'ble High Court ordered immediate de-sealing of the 2 nd floor. It is stated that learned MM has correctly passed the impugned order protecting the Amritesh Jatia vs Vidhi Jatia on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124618478/
5 respondent and children' rights to residence in the shared household and thus, the appeal is liable to be dismissed. In support of her submissions, learned counsel has placed reliance upon the following judgments :
a) Abhijeet Bhikaseth Auti Vs. State of Maharashtra & Anr., 2009 Cri.L.J. 889 b) Moreshar Yadarao Mahajan Vs. Vyankatesh Sitaram Bhedi & Ors., 2022 SCC OnLine SC 1307 c) Prabha Tyagi Vs. Kamlesh Devi (2022) 8 SCC 90 d) Vrinda Ahuja Vs. Raveen Ahuja, 2019 SCC OnLine Del.
11275 e) Niharika Ghosh @ Niharika Kundu Vs. Shankar Ghosh & Anr., CM (M) 431/2023 dated 17.03.2023 7. I have heard arguments of learned senior counsel for appellant as well as of learned counsel for respondent and have perused the record, written submission and judgment cited by both the sides and other material placed on record. 
8. Before proceeding to deal with the matter, it shall be apposite to Amritesh Jatia Vs. Vidhi Jatia &
Anr. Page No.11 of 16 notice the scope of an appeal under Section 29 of the DV Act. Jurisdiction of appellate court under section 29 of DV Act with respect to an order passed under Section 23 of the DV Act is limited to ascertaining if the Trial Court has committed any irregularity or perversity in reaching the finding. This view regarding scope of appeal u/sec.-29 PW DV Act with respect to orders passed u/sec.-23 of PW DV Act was taken by the Hon'ble Bombay High Court in Abhijeet Bhikaseth Auti Vs. State of Maharashtra & Anr. reported as 2009 Crl. Law Journal 889. Relevant portion of the judgment is reproduced herein below:-
"24........... Thus, the conclusion, which can be summarized are as under:
(i)........
(ii)........
(iii) An appeal will also lie against orders passed under sub- section (1) and sub-section (2) of the Section 23 of the said Act which are passed by the learned Magistrate. However, while dealing with an appeal against the order passed under Section 23 of the said Act, the Appellate Court will usually not interfere with the exercise of discretion by the learned Magistrate. The appellate Court will interfere only if it is found that the discretion has been exercised arbitrarily, capriciously, perversely or if it is found that the Court has ignored settled Amritesh Jatia vs Vidhi Jatia on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124618478/
6 principles of law regulating grant or refusal of interim relief."
9. Meaning thereby, this court is to evaluate & assess whether, the Amritesh Jatia Vs. Vidhi Jatia &
Anr. Page No.12 of 16 impugned order suffers from irregularity, lack of exercise of jurisdiction or perversity, etc.
10. Now coming to the present appeal. It is pertinent to mention here that at the time of filing of the appeal, the matter was remanded back to the learned MM for fresh hearing on the point of relief concerning restraining the appellants to refuse food to respondents no.1 and children. Perusal of the trial court record indicates that the matter is still pending adjudication in this regard. 
11. In the present case, the grievance of the appellant is that learned MM without considering the facts and legal provisions and the fact that respondent no.1 has failed to make out a prima facie case for grant of ex-parte relief, passed the impugned order in a mechanical manner and contrary to the principles of natural justice. Besides granting ex-parte relief, the appellant has also been directed to remove all his belongings from 2nd floor of the property. 
12. Perusal of the impugned order indicates that learned MM while passing the impugned order has simply relied upon the application filed by respondent no.1 and observed that she suffered domestic violence at the hands of respondents. The relevant extract of the impugned order is reproduced as under :
"Perusal of the application along with supporting affidavit prima facie shows that complainant was in a domestic relationship with respondents and she suffered domestic violence at the hands of respondents. .... Complainant has Amritesh Jatia Vs. Vidhi Jatia & Anr. Page No.13 of 16 supported allegations of domestic violence with screenshots of conversation that took place between the complainant and respondent no.1. The complainant has also placed reliance on order dated 04.11.2023 of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi, according to which MCD was directed to de-seal the second floor of the property by 05.11.2023...." 
13. From the above, it is evident that learned MM has only considered the allegations made in the application and the documents relied upon by respondent no.1 and passed the impugned order restraining the appellant and his parents from forcibly dispossessing the respondent from the shared household. 
14. The Domestic Violence Act emphasizes the need for a fair hearing. 
Ex-parte relief may be granted in urgent situations, but the principle of natural justice requires that all parties have an opportunity to present their case. The Act does not support granting relief without hearing the respondent unless there is a compelling reason to do so. The court acknowledges the complainant's / respondent's concern regarding her safety and her right to reside in the shared household but at the same time, it cannot be ignored that the appellant has a right to be heard and to defend against the allegations made. 
Amritesh Jatia vs Vidhi Jatia on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124618478/
7 15. In the present case, the respondent no.1's apprehension is that appellant in connivance with MCD officials is trying to dispossess her and the children from the shared household. It may be Amritesh Jatia Vs. Vidhi Jatia & Anr. Page No.14 of 16 mentioned that the appellant himself is a victim of the sealing of the property. Admittedly, his belongings and clothes are lying on 2nd floor. It does not appeal to the reason that why will he intentionally got sealed his valuable items. Thus, the issuance of an ex-parte order directing him to remove his belongings from 2 nd floor of the property without hearing him violates the principles of natural justice. Further, at the time of granting ex-parte relief, the court is required to assess whether the respondent/complainant demonstrated a genuine sense of urgency warranting ex-parte relief. The absence of imminent danger or a credible threat to the respondent's safety raises concerns about the necessity of immediate judicial intervention. The order passed by learned MM appears to reflect a mechanical manner rather than a reasoned approach. 
16. Perusal of the impugned order further shows that learned MM has also failed to consider the ongoing mediation going on between the parties. Learned MM's failure to consider this context suggests that an oversight in evaluating the overall circumstances surrounding the case. 
17. In view of the above findings, the case is remanded back to the learned MM for a thorough re-evaluation of the facts and circumstances of the case. Learned MM is also directed to hear both parties afresh giving them equal opportunity to present their Amritesh Jatia Vs. Vidhi Jatia & Anr.
Page No.15 of 16 case. With these observations, the appeal stands disposed of. The impugned order dated 16.12.2023 is set aside. 
18. Parties are directed to appear before learned trial court on 12.08.2024. 
19. Nothing expressed herein shall tantamount to any expression on the merits of the case. 
20. A copy of this judgment alongwith trial court record be sent back to the learned Trial court. 
21. Appeal file be consigned to Record room. 
Announced in the open court (MADHU JAIN)
